rules.quote: Option 1: GeyserMC's MCProtocolLib RakNet Client (Recommended)
rules.rule: Prefer GeyserMC's MCProtocolLib RakNet client (Option 1) when implementing the Bedrock bot's RakNet client.

rules.quote: Must handle encryption (if server enables it)
rules.rule: The Bedrock bot packet handler must handle encryption when the server enables it.

rules.quote: Must handle encryption (if server enables it) and compression
rules.rule: The Bedrock bot packet handler must handle compression.

rules.quote: **Must use `VarInts.writeInt` (zigzag encoding)** for palette entries and palette size
rules.rule: Use VarInts.writeInt with zigzag encoding when writing palette entries and the palette size.

rules.quote: Use `org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.util.VarInts.writeInt()` directly from the library
rules.rule: Use org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.util.VarInts.writeInt() directly from the library for varint writing.

rules.quote: Client and server must agree on palette order
rules.rule: Ensure that the client and server agree on the block palette order.

rules.quote: use `fromNumber(int, Family...)` for family-aware lookup.
rules.rule: When resolving protocol version numbers that clash between families, use `fromNumber(int, Family...)` for family-aware lookup.

rules.quote: `fromNumber(pv, Family.BETA)` for String16 clients, `fromNumber(pv, Family.ALPHA, Family.BETA)` otherwise.
rules.rule: For String16 clients, resolve the protocol version with `fromNumber(pv, Family.BETA)`; otherwise resolve it with `fromNumber(pv, Family.ALPHA, Family.BETA)`.

rules.quote: C2S damage stays `byte` for phantom KeepAlive compatibility.
rules.rule: For Beta BlockPlacement C2S, keep the damage field as a `byte` to preserve phantom KeepAlive compatibility.

rules.quote: Uses `PlayerBlockPlacementPacketBeta`.
rules.rule: For Beta BlockPlacement packets, use `PlayerBlockPlacementPacketBeta`.

rules.quote: Uses `HoldingChangePacketBeta`.
rules.rule: For Beta HoldingChange packets, use `HoldingChangePacketBeta`.

rules.quote: `SetSlotPacket` uses `writeShort(damage)`/`readShort()`.
rules.rule: In `SetSlotPacket`, write the damage field with `writeShort(damage)` and read it with `readShort()`.

rules.quote: Beta clients use PlayerDigging status=4 for Q-drops instead.
rules.rule: For Beta clients, implement Q-drops with PlayerDigging status=4 instead of using PickupSpawn.

rules.quote: use SetSlot (0x67) to give items.
rules.rule: Give items using SetSlot (0x67) instead of AddToInventory.

rules.quote: per-placement `SetSlot(0, 36, item, 64, 0)` — no batched tracker needed.
rules.rule: Replenish SetSlot per placement using `SetSlot(0, 36, item, 64, 0)`; do not implement a batched tracker.

rules.quote: v7-v11 empty C2S packet; v12+ (Beta 1.6+) adds `byte dimension`.
rules.rule: For Respawn (0x09) C2S, send an empty packet for v7-v11 and add a `byte dimension` field for v12+ (Beta 1.6+).

rules.quote: New C2S packets silently accepted: UseEntity (0x07), CloseWindow (0x65), WindowClick (0x66), ConfirmTransaction (0x6A), UpdateSign (0x82).
rules.rule: Silently accept the C2S packets UseEntity (0x07), CloseWindow (0x65), WindowClick (0x66), ConfirmTransaction (0x6A), and UpdateSign (0x82).

rules.quote: **EntityAction (0x13) C2S**: `[int entityId, byte actionId]`. Registered for all Beta versions.
rules.rule: Register EntityAction (0x13) C2S with the format `[int entityId, byte actionId]` for all Beta versions.

rules.quote: **InputPacket (0x1B) C2S**: 18-byte vehicle steering input, silently consumed. Registered for all Beta versions.
rules.rule: Register InputPacket (0x1B) C2S for all Beta versions and silently consume its 18-byte vehicle steering input.

rules.quote: `RawPacketDecoder`/`RawPacketEncoder` set per-connection via `setUseString16()`.
rules.rule: Set String16 mode per connection in `RawPacketDecoder` and `RawPacketEncoder` using `setUseString16()`.

rules.quote: registered for v11+ via `betaV.getVersionNumber() >= 11`.
rules.rule: Register `WindowClickPacketBeta15` for v11 and above when `betaV.getVersionNumber() >= 11`.

rules.quote: strip ";host:port" suffix.
rules.rule: When parsing a Beta 1.8 handshake in `username;host:port` format, strip the `;host:port` suffix.

rules.quote: Respond with 0xFF + String16("motd§players§max") and close.
rules.rule: For Beta 1.8 server list ping (0xFE), respond with 0xFF followed by String16("motd§players§max") and then close the connection.

rules.quote: **Tick-loop PingPacket must be dropped for v17+**: `dropPing` flag on translator suppresses this.
rules.rule: Drop Tick-loop PingPacket for v17 and above; set the `dropPing` flag on the translator to suppress it.

rules.quote: **Creative mode NOT available until Beta 1.8 (v17)**. All Alpha and Beta 1.0-1.7 require survival-mode hacks.
rules.rule: Do not use creative mode for Alpha or Beta 1.0-1.7; use survival-mode hacks until Beta 1.8 (v17).

rules.quote: Login C2S has NO "unused" String16 field (removed in v17).
rules.rule: In Beta 1.8 (v17) Login C2S, omit the "unused" String16 field.

rules.quote: **0xCA PlayerAbilities does NOT exist in Beta 1.8** — abilities from gameMode in Login/Respawn.
rules.rule: Do not implement PlayerAbilities (0xCA) for Beta 1.8; take abilities from the `gameMode` field in Login/Respawn.

rules.quote: **Beta 1.8 BlockPlacement damage is `short`**: `PlayerBlockPlacementPacketV17` has `short damage` (not `byte`).
rules.rule: For Beta 1.8 (v17) BlockPlacement, use `short damage` in `PlayerBlockPlacementPacketV17`, not `byte`.

rules.quote: New protocol version that drops blocks: add a new YAML
rules.rule: When a new protocol version drops blocks, add a new YAML replacement file.

rules.quote: do NOT touch ServerWorld coercion path.
rules.rule: When a new protocol version drops blocks, do not touch the ServerWorld coercion path.

rules.quote: New protocol version that drops blocks: drop a YAML at `/replacements/<key>.yml`
rules.rule: When a new protocol version drops blocks, drop a YAML file at `/replacements/<key>.yml`.

rules.quote: no code changes.
rules.rule: When a new protocol version drops blocks, make no code changes.

rules.quote: New chokepoint policy (e.g., creative-restricted, claim-protected): write a `BlockPolicy` impl
rules.rule: When adding a new chokepoint policy, such as creative-restricted or claim-protected, write a BlockPolicy implementation.

rules.quote: set via `world.setPolicy(...)`.
rules.rule: When adding a new chokepoint policy, set it via world.setPolicy(...).

rules.quote: Compose with existing policies by chaining inside `coerce`.
rules.rule: When adding a new chokepoint policy, compose it with existing policies by chaining inside coerce.

rules.quote: Do NOT add coercion logic above `ServerWorld.setBlock(byte)`
rules.rule: Never add block coercion logic above ServerWorld.setBlock(byte).

rules.quote: `org.bukkit.block.Biome` in our paper-api stubs (rd-bridge-bukkit) MUST be declared as `public abstract class Biome implements OldEnum, Keyed, Translatable`, NOT as an interface.
rules.rule: In the paper-api stubs (rd-bridge-bukkit), declare `org.bukkit.block.Biome` as `public abstract class Biome implements OldEnum, Keyed, Translatable`, not as an interface.

rules.quote: When auto-generating paper-api stubs, leave `Biome` as a class.
rules.rule: When auto-generating paper-api stubs, leave `Biome` declared as a class.

rules.quote: If Paper upstream changes it, double-check via `javap -c` on a representative plugin (e.g. `com/earth2me/essentials/RandomTeleport.class`, `com/earth2me/essentials/User.class`) whether they emit `invokevirtual` or `invokeinterface` on `Biome.name`.
rules.rule: If Paper upstream changes `Biome`, double-check via `javap -c` on a representative plugin (e.g. `com/earth2me/essentials/RandomTeleport.class`, `com/earth2me/essentials/User.class`) whether the plugin emits `invokevirtual` or `invokeinterface` on `Biome.name`.

rules.quote: Apply the same check to other Bukkit types that flipped between enum/class and interface over the years (e.g. `EntityType`, `Material`, `Particle`, `Statistic`).
rules.rule: Apply the same bytecode check to other Bukkit types that have flipped between enum/class and interface over the years (e.g. `EntityType`, `Material`, `Particle`, `Statistic`).

rules.quote: also keep `BukkitWorldAdapter implements RegionAccessor`
rules.rule: For the same root cause, keep `BukkitWorldAdapter` declared as implementing `RegionAccessor`.

rules.quote: `BukkitPluginWrapper.onEnable` must dispatch `PluginEnableEvent`
rules.rule: BukkitPluginWrapper.onEnable must dispatch PluginEnableEvent via BukkitEventAdapter.dispatchPluginEvent after the plugin's own onEnable() returns.

rules.quote: and `onDisable` must dispatch `PluginDisableEvent`
rules.rule: BukkitPluginWrapper.onDisable must dispatch PluginDisableEvent via BukkitEventAdapter.dispatchPluginEvent after the plugin's own onDisable() returns.

rules.quote: Listeners the plugin registers DURING its own `onEnable` need to receive their own enable event
rules.rule: Listeners that a plugin registers during its own onEnable must receive their own enable event.

rules.quote: Don't drop the dispatch when refactoring `BukkitPluginWrapper`
rules.rule: When refactoring BukkitPluginWrapper, do not drop the PluginEnableEvent dispatch.

rules.quote: order is `plugin.onEnable()` → bridge listeners → `registerCommands` → `dispatchPluginEvent(new PluginEnableEvent(plugin))`
rules.rule: When refactoring BukkitPluginWrapper, preserve the order plugin.onEnable() → bridge listeners → registerCommands → dispatchPluginEvent(new PluginEnableEvent(plugin)).

rules.quote: Don't regenerate them from the auto-stub template
rules.rule: Do not regenerate PluginEvent, PluginEnableEvent, or PluginDisableEvent from the auto-stub template.

rules.quote: When a plugin's behaviour seems to "miss" lifecycle context, suspect this dispatch first.
rules.rule: When a plugin's behaviour seems to miss lifecycle context, suspect the PluginEnableEvent/PluginDisableEvent dispatch first.

rules.quote: Use v1.0.16 (same protocol v14) instead.
rules.rule: When a client JAR for Alpha v1.0.16_02 is needed, use Alpha v1.0.16 (protocol v14) instead, since v1.0.16_02 is only available on OmniArchive.

rules.quote: Use v1.2.0_02 (same protocol v3) instead.
rules.rule: When a client JAR for Alpha v1.2.0 is needed, use Alpha v1.2.0_02 (protocol v3) instead, since v1.2.0 is only available on OmniArchive.

rules.quote: do NOT re-run the entire test suite to debug it
rules.rule: When a test fails during a full suite run, do not re-run the entire test suite to debug it.

rules.quote: Instead, run only the specific failing test class or method
rules.rule: When debugging a failing test, run only the specific failing test class or method rather than the whole suite.

rules.quote: Only run the full suite for final verification after all fixes are applied.
rules.rule: Run the full test suite only for final verification, after all fixes have been applied.

rules.quote: Use `gs.offsetPlayerX(-5.0)` in VerifyGroundStep (settleTicks==0) to nudge player away from column before screenshot.
rules.rule: In VerifyGroundStep, when settleTicks==0, call gs.offsetPlayerX(-5.0) to nudge the player away from the column before taking the screenshot.

rules.quote: Uses direct posX field write (not forcePlayerPosition) to avoid Entity.a()→move() issues on Alpha 1.2.2+.
rules.rule: Use a direct posX field write rather than forcePlayerPosition to move the player, to avoid Entity.a()→move() issues on Alpha 1.2.2+.

rules.quote: Increase wait time in VerifySplitStep or verify item is in correct slot before screenshot.
rules.rule: In VerifySplitStep, either increase the wait time or verify the item is in the correct slot before taking the screenshot.

rules.quote: Add setLookDirection to face the other player before screenshot in cross-test scenario.
rules.rule: In the cross-test scenario, call setLookDirection to make the player face the other player before taking the screenshot.

rules.quote: Needs more wait time.
rules.rule: Increase the wait time before capturing the RD environment_check screenshot so the map is fully rendered.

rules.quote: Stop server
rules.rule: Stop the server before starting the test setup.

rules.quote: delete all map and player data
rules.rule: Delete all map and player data as part of pre-test setup.

rules.quote: Start fresh server
rules.rule: Start a fresh server.

rules.quote: can run 2 servers on different ports for parallel testing
rules.rule: You may run two servers on different ports for parallel testing.

rules.quote: split clients into two halves
rules.rule: When running parallel tests, split clients into two halves.

rules.quote: Each parallel tester has its own client set
rules.rule: Ensure each parallel tester has its own client set.

rules.quote: Performed by the first client logged in.
rules.rule: Have the first client that logs in perform the single-client tests.

rules.quote: Screenshot after every step unless noted.
rules.rule: Take a screenshot after every test step unless the step notes otherwise.

rules.quote: Check chat for "joined the game" message with matching username
rules.rule: Check chat for a "joined the game" message whose username matches the client.

rules.quote: Verify standing on grass block
rules.rule: Verify the client is standing on a grass block.

rules.quote: air in all directions (5 blocks each way: front/back/left/right/top)
rules.rule: Verify there is air in all directions five blocks each way: front, back, left, right, and top.

rules.quote: Verify all chunks loaded
rules.rule: Verify all chunks are loaded.

rules.quote: flat map visible
rules.rule: Verify the flat map is visible.

rules.quote: **Survival-only clients (pre-Beta 1.8)**: Verify 64 cobblestone in inventory
rules.rule: For survival-only clients running pre-Beta 1.8, verify the inventory contains 64 cobblestone.

rules.quote: **Alpha a1.0.15 / a1.0.16 only**: Verify all other inventory slots filled with cooked porkchops
rules.rule: For Alpha a1.0.15 and a1.0.16 only, verify all other inventory slots are filled with cooked porkchops.

rules.quote: Remove grass block to the right
rules.rule: Remove the grass block to the right.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After removing the grass block to the right, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify it's still removed
rules.rule: After waiting 4 seconds, verify the grass block removed to the right is still removed.

rules.quote: Place cobblestone where grass was removed
rules.rule: Place cobblestone where the grass block was removed.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After placing cobblestone where the grass was removed, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify it's placed
rules.rule: After waiting 4 seconds, verify the cobblestone is placed where the grass was removed.

rules.quote: converted to grass
rules.rule: Verify the placed cobblestone is converted to grass.

rules.quote: **Survival-only**: Verify inventory has 64 cobblestone stack (replenishment works)
rules.rule: For survival-only clients, verify the inventory has a 64-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: Place cobblestone next to you to the right
rules.rule: Place cobblestone next to you on the right.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After placing cobblestone next to you to the right, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify it's placed
rules.rule: After waiting 4 seconds, verify the cobblestone placed next to you to the right is present.

rules.quote: Jump on the cobblestone
rules.rule: Jump onto the cobblestone.

rules.quote: look down
rules.rule: Look down.

rules.quote: hold jump + right-click until max height (max 20s timeout)
rules.rule: Hold jump and right-click until reaching max height, with a maximum 20-second timeout.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After reaching max height while holding jump and right-click, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify at map height with cobblestone below feet
rules.rule: Verify you are at map height with cobblestone below your feet.

rules.quote: Hold jump + right-click for 5s more at max height
rules.rule: At max height, hold jump and right-click for 5 more seconds.

rules.quote: stop
rules.rule: Stop holding jump and right-click.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After stopping at max height, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify still at max height
rules.rule: Verify you are still at max height.

rules.quote: Hold left-click until block under feet is grass
rules.rule: Hold left-click until the block under your feet is grass.

rules.quote: wait 4s
rules.rule: After holding left-click until the block under your feet is grass, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify grass below feet
rules.rule: Verify there is grass below your feet.

rules.quote: **Survival-only**: Select 64 cobblestone stack
rules.rule: For survival-only clients, select the 64-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: press Q
rules.rule: Press Q.

rules.quote: verify stack stays at 64
rules.rule: Verify the selected stack stays at 64.

rules.quote: Press T
rules.rule: Press T.

rules.quote: type "HELLO"
rules.rule: Type "HELLO".

rules.quote: Enter
rules.rule: Press Enter.

rules.quote: verify chat shows your name + message
rules.rule: Verify chat shows your name and the message.

rules.quote: Open inventory
rules.rule: Open the inventory.

rules.quote: click empty slot
rules.rule: Click an empty inventory slot.

rules.quote: survival: consume porkchops to free slots first
rules.rule: In survival mode, consume porkchops to free slots before clicking an empty inventory slot.

rules.quote: Creative: grab 64 cobblestone to 2nd quick slot
rules.rule: In creative mode, grab 64 cobblestone into the 2nd quick slot.

rules.quote: Right-click 64-stack
rules.rule: Right-click the 64-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: place 32 on next available slot
rules.rule: Place 32 cobblestone on the next available slot.

rules.quote: verify 2x32 stacks
rules.rule: Verify there are two 32-cobblestone stacks.

rules.quote: Right-click 32-stack
rules.rule: Right-click the 32-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: throw 16 outside inventory
rules.rule: Throw 16 cobblestone outside the inventory.

rules.quote: Alpha: verify 64 total cobblestone (immediate replenish)
rules.rule: For Alpha clients, verify there are 64 total cobblestone after the throw.

rules.quote: Others: verify 1x32 + 1x16
rules.rule: For non-Alpha clients, verify one 32-cobblestone stack and one 16-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: Right-click 32-stack
rules.rule: Right-click the 32-cobblestone stack again.

rules.quote: right-click outside to throw 1 block
rules.rule: Right-click outside the inventory to throw 1 block.

rules.quote: left-click back on origin slot
rules.rule: Left-click back on the origin slot.

rules.quote: Alpha: verify 64 total
rules.rule: For Alpha clients, verify there are 64 total cobblestone.

rules.quote: Others: verify 1x31 + 1x16
rules.rule: For non-Alpha clients, verify one 31-cobblestone stack and one 16-cobblestone stack.

rules.quote: Close inventory
rules.rule: Close the inventory.

rules.quote: Beta: verify only 1x64 cobblestone stack and nothing else
rules.rule: For Beta clients, verify there is only one 64-cobblestone stack and nothing else in the inventory.

rules.quote: Alpha: verify 64 total cobblestone
rules.rule: For Alpha clients, verify there are 64 total cobblestone in the inventory.

rules.quote: Walk/fly to map edge (detect non-air 10 blocks ahead)
rules.rule: Walk or fly to the map edge by detecting non-air 10 blocks ahead.

rules.quote: walk into void
rules.rule: Walk into the void at the map edge.

rules.quote: verify falling at 10+ blocks/sec
rules.rule: Verify you are falling at 10 or more blocks per second.

rules.quote: when below Y=-10 wait 4s
rules.rule: When below Y=-10, wait 4 seconds.

rules.quote: verify teleported back to spawn with grass below feet
rules.rule: Verify you are teleported back to spawn with grass below your feet.

rules.quote: Place 1 block from each inventory slot in a row (max 80 per row, then start new row 3 blocks behind)
rules.rule: In creative mode, place one block from each inventory slot in a row, starting a new row 3 blocks behind after 80 blocks.

rules.quote: verify each block converts to cobblestone
rules.rule: Verify each placed block converts to cobblestone.

rules.quote: non-block items disappear within 4s
rules.rule: Verify non-block items disappear within 4 seconds.

rules.quote: some items do nothing or trigger actions — that's OK
rules.rule: Accept that some items may do nothing or trigger actions.

rules.quote: walk to start
rules.rule: After placing all blocks, walk to the start.

rules.quote: face placed blocks
rules.rule: Face the placed blocks.

rules.quote: jump onto first block
rules.rule: Jump onto the first placed block.

rules.quote: screenshot
rules.rule: Take a screenshot after jumping onto the first placed block.

rules.quote: Return to spawn point
rules.rule: Return to the spawn point.

rules.quote: After single-client tests, test interaction with every other available client version.
rules.rule: After completing single-client tests, test interaction with every other available client version.

rules.quote: Initialize internal counter at 1
rules.rule: Initialize the internal counter at 1.

rules.quote: Start next client from the full test list
rules.rule: Start the next client from the full test list.

rules.quote: offline mode
rules.rule: Start the next client in offline mode.

rules.quote: username "Tester X"
rules.rule: Use the username "Tester X" for the next client, where X is the counter.

rules.quote: increment after start
rules.rule: Increment the counter after starting the client.

rules.quote: log into same server
rules.rule: Log the next client into the same server.

rules.quote: Walk 3 steps back
rules.rule: Walk 3 steps back.

rules.quote: rotate to face the other player
rules.rule: Rotate to face the other player.

rules.quote: Client 2 presses T
rules.rule: Have Client 2 press T.

rules.quote: types "HERE I AM"
rules.rule: Have Client 2 type "HERE I AM".

rules.quote: Enter
rules.rule: Have Client 2 press Enter.

rules.quote: verify both clients see the message (2 screenshots, low similarity threshold for username variance)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the message by taking 2 screenshots and using a low similarity threshold for username variance.

rules.quote: Client 1 presses T
rules.rule: Have Client 1 press T.

rules.quote: types "I SEE YOU"
rules.rule: Have Client 1 type "I SEE YOU".

rules.quote: Enter
rules.rule: Have Client 1 press Enter.

rules.quote: verify both clients see the message (2 screenshots)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the message by taking 2 screenshots.

rules.quote: Client 1 places block to the right
rules.rule: Have Client 1 place a block to the right.

rules.quote: verify both clients see the placed block (2 screenshots)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the placed block by taking 2 screenshots.

rules.quote: Client 1 destroys that block
rules.rule: Have Client 1 destroy that block.

rules.quote: verify both clients see block removed (2 screenshots)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the block removed by taking 2 screenshots.

rules.quote: Client 2 places block to the right
rules.rule: Have Client 2 place a block to the right.

rules.quote: verify both clients see the placed block (2 screenshots)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the placed block by taking 2 screenshots.

rules.quote: Client 2 destroys that block
rules.rule: Have Client 2 destroy that block.

rules.quote: verify both clients see block removed (2 screenshots)
rules.rule: Verify both clients see the block removed by taking 2 screenshots.

rules.quote: Close client 2
rules.rule: Close Client 2.

rules.quote: Repeat steps 23-31 for every remaining client in the test list
rules.rule: Repeat steps 23 through 31 for every remaining client in the test list.

rules.quote: Run: `./gradlew :rd-e2e:test -Pe2e` (skipped during normal builds)
rules.rule: Run the E2E test suite with `./gradlew :rd-e2e:test -Pe2e`; the task is skipped during normal builds.

rules.quote: **Timeouts**: 120-150 minutes for pre-1.19 (`test` task), 120-150 minutes for 1.19+ (`testModern` task). 30 minutes is NOT enough.
rules.rule: When configuring E2E test timeouts, allow 120-150 minutes for pre-1.19 (`test`) and 120-150 minutes for 1.19+ (`testModern`); do not use a 30-minute timeout.

rules.quote: Do NOT remove.
rules.rule: Do not remove the intentional beta inventory `resetInventory`-on-close behavior that resets all slots to 1x64 cobblestone.

rules.quote: Solution: use exact field names, not type fallback.
rules.rule: For Alpha 1.2.6 Entity position fields, use exact field names instead of the type-scan fallback.

rules.quote: **All shared fields MUST be `public static volatile`**
rules.rule: Declare all shared ByteBuddy agent fields as `public static volatile`.

rules.quote: **Use `Advice`, not `MethodDelegation`**
rules.rule: Use ByteBuddy `Advice` instead of `MethodDelegation`.

rules.quote: Movement: write directly to `he.f[]` boolean array via reflection (no KeyBinding.pressed in Alpha)
rules.rule: For movement input in Alpha, write directly to the `he.f[]` boolean array via reflection rather than using KeyBinding.pressed.

rules.quote: Mouse clicks: call `Minecraft.a(int)` via reflection (0=left, 1=right)
rules.rule: Inject mouse clicks in Alpha by calling `Minecraft.a(int)` via reflection, with 0 for left and 1 for right.

rules.quote: Look direction: set Entity.yaw/pitch directly
rules.rule: Set Entity.yaw and Entity.pitch directly to control look direction.

rules.quote: Set to 10 when objectMouseOver is null.
rules.rule: Set the `Minecraft.S` click-cooldown field to 10 when objectMouseOver is null.

rules.quote: Reset to 0 before left-clicks.
rules.rule: Reset the `Minecraft.S` click-cooldown field to 0 before left-clicks.

rules.quote: Use `PlayerController.b.a(int,int,int,int)` to bypass Minecraft.a(0) cooldown/objectMouseOver checks.
rules.rule: Use `PlayerController.b.a(int,int,int,int)` direct dig packets to bypass `Minecraft.a(0)` cooldown and objectMouseOver checks.

rules.quote: Use direct dig packets instead of click(0) for reliable breaking.
rules.rule: Use direct dig packets instead of click(0) for reliable block breaking.

rules.quote: **NEVER run 2 concurrent Gradle test runs.**
rules.rule: Never run two concurrent Gradle test runs.

rules.quote: **ALWAYS use `fatJar` task** (not `jar`) when rebuilding the e2e agent.
rules.rule: Always use the `fatJar` task, not `jar`, when rebuilding the e2e agent.

rules.quote: ALWAYS read the scenario source code before assuming what a screenshot should look like.
rules.rule: Before assuming what a screenshot should look like, always read the scenario source code.

rules.quote: Do NOT guess from the screenshot file name alone.
rules.rule: Do not guess what a screenshot should look like from the screenshot file name alone.

rules.quote: All other fields (posX, inventoryFieldName, creativeInventoryClassName, etc.) must come from the correct mapping file.
rules.rule: For Minecraft sub-version mappings, take all fields other than `minecraftClassName`, `runMethodName`, and `tickMethodName` from the correct mapping file.

rules.quote: Must extract individual .class files first (CFR decompiles entire JAR otherwise)
rules.rule: Extract individual `.class` files before running CFR on them, because CFR otherwise decompiles the entire JAR.

rules.quote: Bypass jemalloc via system malloc.
rules.rule: When running MC 1.17+ with LWJGL under Java 17+, bypass jemalloc by using system malloc (for example, `-Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system`).

rules.quote: Force Mesa to report GL 4.5 Compatibility Profile.
rules.rule: When running MC 1.17+ under Mesa, force Mesa to report GL 4.5 Compatibility Profile (for example, with `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=4.5COMPAT`).

rules.quote: Download: `curl -fSL -o /tmp/cfr.jar "https://github.com/leibnitz27/cfr/releases/download/0.152/cfr-0.152.jar"`
rules.rule: Download CFR 0.152 to `/tmp/cfr.jar` using `curl -fSL -o /tmp/cfr.jar https://github.com/leibnitz27/cfr/releases/download/0.152/cfr-0.152.jar`.

rules.quote: Usage: `jar xf client.jar ClassName.class && java -jar /tmp/cfr.jar ClassName.class`
rules.rule: To decompile a class with CFR, extract the individual `.class` file from the client JAR and run CFR on that file.

rules.quote: Not breaking existing clients is the HIGHEST PRIORITY constraint.
rules.rule: Treat not breaking existing clients as the highest-priority constraint.

rules.quote: This takes precedence over clean code, performance, and new features.
rules.rule: Prioritize backwards compatibility over clean code, performance, and new features.

rules.quote: Every code change — adding new protocol versions, refactoring shared code, or fixing bugs — MUST preserve full compatibility with ALL previously supported clients.
rules.rule: Ensure every code change, including adding protocol versions, refactoring shared code, and fixing bugs, preserves full compatibility with all previously supported clients.

rules.quote: If a shared method is used by multiple protocol versions, NEVER change its behavior globally.
rules.rule: If a shared method is used by multiple protocol versions, never change its behavior globally.

rules.quote: Add a version parameter and branch, or create a version-specific override.
rules.rule: When a shared method must differ by protocol version, add a version parameter and branch, or create a version-specific override.

rules.quote: Before editing any shared code, trace ALL callers to verify which clients are affected.
rules.rule: Before editing any shared code, trace all callers to verify which clients are affected.

rules.quote: Guard new behavior behind version checks so only the targeted client type is affected.
rules.rule: Guard new behavior behind version checks so only the targeted client type is affected.

rules.quote: After any change to packet handling, test at least one client from each supported version range.
rules.rule: After any change to packet handling, test at least one client from each supported version range.

rules.quote: When adding version thresholds (e.g. `if (version >= V27)`), verify the threshold is correct for ALL versions in the affected range.
rules.rule: When adding version thresholds, verify the threshold is correct for all versions in the affected range.

rules.quote: The user expects to be told about regressions proactively, not discover them during testing.
rules.rule: Tell the user about regressions proactively rather than letting the user discover them during testing.

rules.quote: Before signaling that a server-side change is ready for the user to test manually, ALWAYS run `./gradlew buildAll`
rules.rule: Always run `./gradlew buildAll` before signaling that a server-side change is ready for the user to test manually.

rules.quote: Per-module tasks like `:rd-bridge-bukkit:compileJava` are not enough — the user launches the fat jar.
rules.rule: Do not rely on per-module build tasks such as `:rd-bridge-bukkit:compileJava` alone to prepare a server-side change for testing, since the user launches the fat jar.

rules.quote: After any code change in any module that ships inside the server fat jar (rd-api, rd-protocol, rd-world, rd-server, rd-bridge-*, rd-mod-loader), run `./gradlew buildAll`
rules.rule: After any code change in a module that ships inside the server fat jar (rd-api, rd-protocol, rd-world, rd-server, rd-bridge-*, rd-mod-loader), run `./gradlew buildAll`.

rules.quote: confirm `rd-server-0.2.0-SNAPSHOT-all.jar` exists under `rd-server/build/libs/` before asking for a retest
rules.rule: Confirm that `rd-server-0.2.0-SNAPSHOT-all.jar` exists under `rd-server/build/libs/` before asking the user for a retest.

rules.quote: Test-only changes (e.g. `src/test/java`) are exempt.
rules.rule: Test-only changes (e.g. under `src/test/java`) are exempt from the requirement to run `./gradlew buildAll` before requesting a retest.

rules.quote: If new E2E tests fail with "[SpawnProtection] Blocked" in logs, verify E2ETestServer is writing server.properties before start.
rules.rule: When a new E2E test fails and the logs contain "[SpawnProtection] Blocked", verify that E2ETestServer writes server.properties before the server starts.

rules.quote: No per-test changes needed — the fix is in E2ETestServer.start().
rules.rule: Do not make per-test changes to fix spawn protection; the fix belongs in E2ETestServer.start().

rules.quote: Lazy-load all protocol infrastructure
rules.rule: Lazy-load all protocol infrastructure.

rules.quote: decouple version-specific code branches
rules.rule: Decouple version-specific code branches.

rules.quote: No protocol adapter should be loaded until a client of that type actually connects.
rules.rule: Do not load any protocol adapter until a client of that type actually connects.

rules.quote: Version-specific if-else chains in shared handlers should be extracted into codec/strategy classes selected at connection time.
rules.rule: Extract version-specific if-else chains in shared handlers into codec or strategy classes selected at connection time.

rules.quote: Use JVM inner-class holders for static registries
rules.rule: Use JVM inner-class holders for static registries.

rules.quote: Use synchronized lazy getters (volatile + double-checked locking) for instance-level deferred init, following `BedrockProtocolConstants` as the reference pattern
rules.rule: Use synchronized lazy getters with volatile and double-checked locking for instance-level deferred initialization, following `BedrockProtocolConstants` as the reference pattern.

rules.quote: Extract version-specific wire format logic from shared methods into codec classes selected per-session at connection time
rules.rule: Extract version-specific wire format logic from shared methods into codec classes selected per session at connection time.

rules.quote: Broadcast methods dispatching to mixed-version recipients must use the RECIPIENT's codec, not the sender's
rules.rule: When broadcast methods dispatch to mixed-version recipients, use the recipient's codec, not the sender's codec.

rules.quote: Applies to ALL protocol types: TCP, MCPE, Bedrock, and any future protocols
rules.rule: Apply these lazy-loading and decoupling rules to all protocol types: TCP, MCPE, Bedrock, and any future protocols.

rules.quote: NEVER delete or reset world save files (server-world.dat, server-players.dat, or similar) without explicit user permission.
rules.rule: Never delete world save files such as server-world.dat, server-players.dat, or similar without explicit user permission.

rules.quote: NEVER delete or reset world save files (server-world.dat, server-players.dat, or similar) without explicit user permission.
rules.rule: Never reset world save files such as server-world.dat, server-players.dat, or similar without explicit user permission.

rules.quote: Before ANY destructive file operation (rm, overwrite, reset) on data files in the project root, ALWAYS ask the user first. This applies to world saves, player data, configuration, and any non-code files that may contain user-generated state.
rules.rule: Before any destructive file operation (rm, overwrite, reset) on data files in the project root—including world saves, player data, configuration, and any non-code files that may contain user-generated state—always ask the user first.

rules.quote: If you need a clean world for testing, ask the user to confirm before deleting.
rules.rule: If you need a clean world for testing, ask the user to confirm before deleting.

rules.quote: Do not start or restart the RDForward server process unless the user gives implicit or explicit permission.
rules.rule: Do not start or restart the RDForward server process unless the user gives implicit or explicit permission.

rules.quote: After building, do NOT automatically start the server.
rules.rule: After building, do not automatically start the server.

rules.quote: Only start it when the user says something like "start the server", "let's test it", "fire it up", or otherwise indicates they want it running.
rules.rule: Only start the server when the user indicates they want it running, such as by saying "start the server", "let's test it", or "fire it up".

rules.quote: The same applies to restarts after rebuilds.
rules.rule: Do not restart the server after rebuilds unless the user indicates they want it running.

rules.quote: Do not start or restart the RDForward server process unless the user gives implicit or explicit permission.
rules.rule: Do not start or restart the RDForward server process unless the user gives implicit or explicit permission.

rules.quote: After building, do NOT automatically start the server.
rules.rule: After building, do not automatically start the server.

rules.quote: Only start it when the user says something like "start the server", "let's test it", "fire it up", or otherwise indicates they want it running.
rules.rule: Start the RDForward server only when the user asks for it to run, such as by saying "start the server", "let's test it", or "fire it up", or otherwise indicates they want it running.

rules.quote: The same applies to restarts after rebuilds.
rules.rule: Do not automatically restart the server after rebuilds unless the user permits it.

rules.quote: Always start the server using a plain Bash `&` background, exactly as documented in CLAUDE.md.
rules.rule: Start the RDForward server using a plain Bash `&` background invocation, following the method documented in CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: Never use `run_in_background: true` for the server process.
rules.rule: Never use `run_in_background: true` when starting the server process.

rules.quote: When starting the server, use a single Bash tool call:
rules.rule: When starting the server, issue it as a single Bash tool call.

rules.quote: Then wait a few seconds
rules.rule: After starting the server, wait a few seconds before checking its output.

rules.quote: check logs with `cat /tmp/rdforward-server.log`.
rules.rule: After starting the server, check its logs using `cat /tmp/rdforward-server.log`.

rules.quote: do NOT draw conclusions from timed log checks or notifications
rules.rule: When waiting for the user to test something, do not draw conclusions from timed log checks or notifications.

rules.quote: Wait for the user to explicitly confirm they have tried before analyzing results.
rules.rule: When waiting for the user to test something, wait for the user to explicitly confirm they have tried it before analyzing results.

rules.quote: wait for their explicit "I tried" / result message before checking logs
rules.rule: After asking the user to test something, wait for their explicit "I tried" or result message before checking logs.

rules.quote: wait for their explicit "I tried" / result message before checking logs or suggesting fixes
rules.rule: After asking the user to test something, wait for their explicit "I tried" or result message before suggesting fixes.

rules.quote: Do not schedule timed checks
rules.rule: Do not schedule timed checks.

rules.quote: Do not schedule timed checks and assume lack of data means a problem.
rules.rule: Do not assume that a lack of data means there is a problem.

rules.quote: Don't change their ids.
rules.rule: Do not change the pre-Flattening block ids of the 19 protected modern Material names (AIR, STONE, GRASS_BLOCK, DIRT, COBBLESTONE, OAK_PLANKS, OAK_SAPLING, BEDROCK, WATER, LAVA, SAND, GRAVEL, GOLD_ORE, IRON_ORE, COAL_ORE, OAK_LOG, OAK_LEAVES, GLASS, TNT).

rules.quote: don't conflate.
rules.rule: Do not conflate BED (the item, id 355) with BED_BLOCK (the placed block, id 26); treat them according to pre-Flattening semantics.

rules.quote: File header keeps `@rdforward:preserve`
rules.rule: Keep `@rdforward:preserve` in the Material.java file header.

rules.quote: Don't blindly regenerate.
rules.rule: Do not blindly regenerate Material.java; preserve the hand-tuned helper methods and protected-id overrides.

rules.quote: re-run `/tmp/gen_material.py` against fresh Paper source
rules.rule: When adding new entries from a Paper update, re-run `/tmp/gen_material.py` against the fresh Paper source.

rules.quote: diff
rules.rule: When adding new entries from a Paper update, diff the generated Material output.

rules.quote: append new entries
rules.rule: When adding new entries from a Paper update, append the new entries to Material.java.

rules.quote: MCPE C2S MovePlayer Y = feet-level; internal server Y = eye-level (feet + 1.62)
rules.rule: Treat MCPE C2S MovePlayer Y as feet-level and the internal server Y as eye-level (feet + 1.62).

rules.quote: MCPE yaw 0 = South; Classic yaw 0 = North; offset = +180 degrees (128 bytes)
rules.rule: When converting yaw between MCPE and Classic, treat MCPE yaw 0 as South and Classic yaw 0 as North, applying an offset of +180 degrees (128 bytes).

rules.quote: AddPlayer/StartGame/MovePlayer S2C Y = feet-level
rules.rule: Send AddPlayer, StartGame, and MovePlayer S2C Y at feet-level.

rules.quote: splitId uses separate counter (`session.nextSplitId()`), NOT sequence number counter
rules.rule: Use a separate splitId counter (`session.nextSplitId()`), not the sequence number counter.

rules.quote: Shared ordering index across all fragments of a split packet
rules.rule: Use a shared ordering index across all fragments of a split packet.

rules.quote: Sequence number allocated only when actually sending (not wasted on fragments)
rules.rule: Allocate a sequence number only when actually sending, not for fragments.

rules.quote: One section per packet (PocketMine Alpha_1.3 `getOrderedMiniChunk()` style)
rules.rule: Send one section per packet, using the PocketMine Alpha_1.3 `getOrderedMiniChunk()` style.

rules.quote: 8 packets per chunk (sections 0-7)
rules.rule: Send 8 packets per chunk, covering sections 0 through 7.

rules.quote: Per-column per-section data: flag byte + 16 block IDs + 8 metadata nibble bytes
rules.rule: Encode per-column per-section data as a flag byte, 16 block IDs, and 8 metadata nibble bytes.

rules.quote: Flag = `(1 << sectionIndex)` with exactly one bit set
rules.rule: Set the flag to `(1 << sectionIndex)` with exactly one bit set.

rules.quote: Uses RubyDung palette: grass (ID 2) at surface Y, cobblestone (ID 4) everywhere else
rules.rule: Use the RubyDung palette: grass (ID 2) at surface Y and cobblestone (ID 4) everywhere else.

rules.quote: **Workaround**: Server-side raycast on arm swing
rules.rule: When the client sends an arm swing (AnimatePacket), perform a server-side raycast.

rules.quote: raycasts from player eye position along look direction
rules.rule: Raycast from the player's eye position along the look direction.

rules.quote: breaks first non-air block within 5-block reach
rules.rule: Break the first non-air block within 5-block reach.

rules.quote: 300ms cooldown between breaks
rules.rule: Enforce a 300ms cooldown between breaks.

rules.quote: Uses Classic yaw convention (0=North) from `floatYaw`
rules.rule: Use the Classic yaw convention (0=North) from `floatYaw`.

rules.quote: Block breaking: still uses raycast workaround (same as 0.7.0)
rules.rule: For protocol 12, continue using the same raycast workaround for block breaking as in 0.7.0.

rules.quote: Accepts ONLY protocol 27 (no range).
rules.rule: Only accept clients using protocol 27; do not accept a range of protocol versions.

rules.quote: All multi-byte fields use big-endian wire encoding.
rules.rule: Encode all multi-byte fields using big-endian wire encoding.

rules.quote: Speed fields ARE required (omitting them shifts all subsequent fields by 12 bytes)
rules.rule: Always include the speedX, speedY, and speedZ fields when writing AddPlayerPacket (0x07).

rules.quote: Workaround: resend entire chunk via FullChunkData after block changes
rules.rule: After a block change, resend the entire chunk via FullChunkData instead of relying on UpdateBlockPacket.

rules.quote: STOP_BREAK should be ignored (prevents double-break)
rules.rule: Ignore STOP_BREAK actions to prevent double-break.

rules.quote: 300ms cooldown between breaks
rules.rule: Enforce a 300ms cooldown between block breaks.

rules.quote: Raycast (Animate handler) disabled for v14+
rules.rule: Disable the raycast Animate handler for protocol v14 and above, since those clients send PlayerAction.

rules.quote: PlayStatus(LOGIN_SUCCESS) MUST be standalone.
rules.rule: When sending packets to a v45 client during early login, send PlayStatus(LOGIN_SUCCESS) as a standalone packet, not batched.

rules.quote: Use REMOVE_ENTITY (0x0C) instead for player despawn.
rules.rule: For player despawn, use REMOVE_ENTITY (0x0C) instead of REMOVE_PLAYER.

rules.quote: extract displayName from extraData.
rules.rule: When parsing the chain JSON, extract displayName from extraData.

rules.quote: toWireId: canonical >= 0xA9 → wire = canonical - 1.
rules.rule: When converting a canonical packet ID to a v9 wire ID, if the canonical ID is >= 0xA9, set the wire ID to the canonical ID minus 1.

rules.quote: toCanonicalId: wire >= 0xA8 → canonical = wire + 1.
rules.rule: When converting a v9 wire packet ID to a canonical ID, if the wire ID is >= 0xA8, set the canonical ID to the wire ID plus 1.

rules.quote: Send with zero entries for no packs.
rules.rule: When sending the ResourcePacksInfo packet and there are no resource packs to offer, send it with zero pack entries.

rules.quote: Same as pre-Netty: `short(-1)` for no NBT, `short(len) + byte[len]` for present. NOT `byte(0x00)` TAG_End as wiki.vg incorrectly suggests.
rules.rule: For Release 1.7.2 slot data NBT, encode absent NBT as short(-1) and present NBT as short(len)+byte[len]; do not use byte(0x00) TAG_End.

rules.quote: After cipher install, send LoginSuccessPacket directly.
rules.rule: In the 1.7.2 login flow, after installing the AES/CFB8 ciphers, send LoginSuccessPacket directly instead of an empty S2C EncryptionKeyResponse.

rules.quote: SpawnPlayer (0x0C) has NO properties list
rules.rule: When serializing the 1.7.2 SpawnPlayer packet (0x0C), omit the properties list.

rules.quote: We write `VarInt(0)`.
rules.rule: For 1.7.6 SpawnPlayer (0x0C), write VarInt(0) for the properties count.

rules.quote: Must send ADD_PLAYER before SpawnPlayer (client resolves name from tab list).
rules.rule: When spawning a player for 1.8 clients, send PlayerListItem ADD_PLAYER before SpawnPlayer so the client can resolve the name from the tab list.

rules.quote: `ClassicToNettyTranslator.setClientVersion()` MUST be called BEFORE `broadcastPlayerListAdd()` and `broadcastPlayerSpawn()` in `handleJoinGame()`.
rules.rule: In handleJoinGame(), call ClassicToNettyTranslator.setClientVersion() before broadcastPlayerListAdd() and broadcastPlayerSpawn().

rules.quote: **Uses global palette mode (bitsPerBlock=13)**: Raw global block state IDs packed directly in data array. No section palette.
rules.rule: When serializing 1.9 chunks, use global palette mode with bitsPerBlock=13 and raw global block state IDs in the data array; do not use a section palette.

rules.quote: **Block entity count is version-specific**: v107-v109 have NO block entity field (packet ends after data); v110 (1.9.4+) appends VarInt blockEntityCount + NBT compounds.
rules.rule: When serializing 1.9 chunks, omit the block entity count for v107-v109; for v110+ append VarInt blockEntityCount followed by NBT compounds.

rules.quote: Cursor positions are **unsigned bytes** (3 × 1 byte), same as pre-1.9. Cursor positions became floats in a later version (1.11+), NOT 1.9.
rules.rule: For 1.9 BlockPlacement, encode cursor positions as three unsigned bytes; do not use floats, which were introduced in 1.11+.

rules.quote: Handler subtracts `PLAYER_EYE_HEIGHT` from internal eye-level Y for 1.8+ clients in both `handleJoinGame()` and `respawnToSafePosition()`.
rules.rule: For 1.8+ clients, subtract PLAYER_EYE_HEIGHT from the internal eye-level Y when sending player position in both handleJoinGame() and respawnToSafePosition().

rules.quote: MUST register FULL C2S forward map (54 entries) — sparse registration causes wrong packet handlers via cascade.
rules.rule: For 1.20.2 (v764), register the full 54-entry C2S forward packet map; do not use sparse registration because it causes wrong packet handlers via cascade.

rules.quote: ALL sent S2C packets need explicit v764 reverse entries — cascade to v762 gives wrong IDs.
rules.rule: For 1.20.2 (v764), add explicit reverse entries for every S2C packet the server sends; do not rely on cascade to v762, which gives wrong IDs.

rules.quote: RegistryData biome entry must have `id=1` (plains) to match chunk serialization which writes biome palette value 1. id=0 causes invisible chunks.
rules.rule: In v764 RegistryData, set the plains biome entry id to 1 to match chunk serialization's biome palette value 1; id=0 causes invisible chunks.

rules.quote: **CRITICAL: NOT per-entry format**: The per-entry format (String registryId + VarInt count + entries with Optional<CompoundTag>) was introduced in 1.20.5 (v766), NOT 1.20.2.
rules.rule: For 1.20.2-1.20.4 RegistryData, do not use the per-entry format (String registryId + VarInt count + entries with Optional<CompoundTag>); that format was introduced in 1.20.5 (v766).

rules.quote: Network NBT (1.20.2+): ALL NBT over the network omits root compound name. Root = 0x0A + children + 0x00 (no writeShort(0) for name).
rules.rule: For 1.20.2+ network NBT, omit the root compound name: write tag id 0x0A, the children, and 0x00, without a writeShort(0) name.

rules.quote: Setting hasData=false tells client to use built-in data. This is REQUIRED for dimension_type and biome — custom data causes CONFIG hang (client never sends ConfigFinishC2S).
rules.rule: In v766 RegistryData, set hasData=false for dimension_type and biome so the client uses built-in data; custom data causes a CONFIG hang because the client never sends ConfigFinishC2S.

rules.quote: Chunks use biome palette value 1 for plains, so send the_void at index 0 and plains at index 1.
rules.rule: In the v766 biome registry, send the_void at index 0 and plains at index 1 so the plains entry's position-based ID is 1, matching the chunk biome palette value.

rules.quote: Pad with empty sections: 4 prepended (Y -64 to -1), 16 existing (Y 0-255), 4 appended (Y 256-319).
rules.rule: For v766 chunk data with the built-in overworld, pad to 24 sections: 4 empty sections prepended, the 16 existing sections, and 4 empty sections appended.

rules.quote: **Heightmap offset**: Add 64 to all heightmap values (minY shifted from 0 to -64).
rules.rule: In v766 chunk data, add 64 to all heightmap values because minY shifted from 0 to -64.

rules.quote: **Light mask shift**: Shift left by 4 bits (sections 0-7 move to positions 4-11 in 26-bit range).
rules.rule: In v766 chunk data, shift the light mask left by 4 bits so sections 0-7 map to positions 4-11 in the 26-bit range.

rules.quote: After LoginAcknowledged, server sends SelectKnownPacksS2CPacket (CONFIG 0x0E) with `minecraft:core v1.20.5`.
rules.rule: In v766, after LoginAcknowledged, send SelectKnownPacksS2CPacket (CONFIG 0x0E) with minecraft:core v1.20.5, then send registries the client lacks built-in after the client replies.

rules.quote: **BlockPlacement (USE_ITEM_ON) gained worldBorderHit**: `NettyBlockPlacementPacketV768`. Boolean `worldBorderHit` inserted between `isInsideBlock` and `sequence`.
rules.rule: For v768 BlockPlacement (USE_ITEM_ON), insert the boolean worldBorderHit between isInsideBlock and sequence.

rules.quote: **PlayerInput (SteerVehicle) rewritten**: `PlayerInputPacketV768`. Old: float sideways + float forward + byte flags (9 bytes). New: byte flags (1 byte). Flags: forward(0x01), backward(0x02), left(0x04), right(0x08), jump(0x10), sneak(0x20), sprint(0x40).
rules.rule: For v768 PlayerInput (SteerVehicle), encode the packet as a single byte flags field; do not use the old float sideways + float forward + byte flags format.

rules.quote: **Heightmaps binary format**: Replaced NBT compound with `VarInt count + [VarInt typeId + VarInt longCount + long[]]`. Type ordinals: WORLD_SURFACE=1, MOTION_BLOCKING=4.
rules.rule: For v770 chunk heightmaps, use the binary format VarInt count + [VarInt typeId + VarInt longCount + long[]] instead of an NBT compound.

rules.quote: **Section palette data arrays**: VarInt length prefix REMOVED.
rules.rule: In v770 chunk section palette data arrays, omit the VarInt length prefix.

rules.quote: **channeling enchantment's built-in data references block tag `#minecraft:lightning_rods` — this tag MUST exist or client fails to parse enchantment registry.**
rules.rule: For v773, ensure the block tag #minecraft:lightning_rods exists because the channeling enchantment's built-in data references it; otherwise the client fails to parse the enchantment registry.

rules.quote: **SpawnEntity wire format changed**: Velocity field changed from 3 shorts (6 bytes) to MOVEMENT_VECTOR encoding. Field reordered: velocity now between position (x,y,z) and rotation (pitch,yaw,headYaw), was previously at end after data. Zero velocity = single byte 0x00.
rules.rule: For v773 SpawnEntity, encode velocity as a MOVEMENT_VECTOR (zero velocity = single byte 0x00) and place it between position and rotation, not at the end after data.

rules.quote: **SpawnPosition wire format changed**: GlobalBlockPosition format — `String dimension + Position (packed long) + float yaw + float pitch`.
rules.rule: For v773 SpawnPosition, use the GlobalBlockPosition format: String dimension + Position (packed long) + float yaw + float pitch.

rules.quote: **No tag changes**. Reuse UpdateTagsPacketV771.
rules.rule: For v772, reuse UpdateTagsPacketV771 because there are no tag changes.

rules.quote: **Offline mode serverId MUST be `"-"`** (not `""`).
rules.rule: For v39 offline mode, set serverId to `"-"`, not an empty string.

rules.quote: **PreChunk (0x32) still required for v28/v29**.
rules.rule: For protocol versions v28 and v29, still include the PreChunk (0x32) packet.

rules.quote: **Entity Properties S2C REQUIRED**: `generic.movementSpeed = 0.10000000149011612`.
rules.rule: For protocol v73, include the required S2C Entity Properties packet with generic.movementSpeed set to 0.10000000149011612.

rules.quote: runMethodName=`d` (not `run`)
rules.rule: When configuring the end-to-end agent, set runMethodName to `d`, not `run`.

rules.quote: serverHostFieldName=null
rules.rule: When configuring the end-to-end agent, set serverHostFieldName to null.

rules.quote: bots must use `sendPacketImmediately()` for reliable delivery in tests.
rules.rule: When sending Bedrock client-to-server packets in bot tests, use `sendPacketImmediately()` instead of the batched `sendPacket()` to ensure reliable delivery.

rules.quote: `PrioritizedEvent<T>` **extends** `Event<T>` and preserves `invoker()` pattern (plan's `fire(Function, BiConsumer)` is discarded)
rules.rule: Implement PrioritizedEvent<T> as a subclass of Event<T> that preserves the invoker() pattern and discards the plan's fire(Function, BiConsumer) method.

rules.quote: Stop-on-cancel happens inside the invoker loop: iterate priorities LOWEST→HIGHEST, break on FAIL, then always run MONITOR list (return values ignored)
rules.rule: Implement stop-on-cancel inside the invoker loop by iterating priorities from LOWEST to HIGHEST, breaking on FAIL, and then always running the MONITOR list while ignoring its return values.

rules.quote: `ServerEvents` migrates fully to `PrioritizedEvent<T>`
rules.rule: Migrate ServerEvents fully to PrioritizedEvent<T>.

rules.quote: existing `.register(T)` and `.invoker()` callers unchanged
rules.rule: Keep existing .register(T) and .invoker() callers unchanged when migrating ServerEvents to PrioritizedEvent<T>.

rules.quote: Fabric bridge upcasts `PrioritizedEvent<T>` to `Event<T>`
rules.rule: Have the Fabric bridge upcast PrioritizedEvent<T> to Event<T>.

rules.quote: Mods wanting priority use new `register(EventPriority, T)` overload
rules.rule: Provide a new register(EventPriority, T) overload for mods that want to register with priority.

rules.quote: MONITOR listeners read cancelled-state via ThreadLocal set during dispatch
rules.rule: Make MONITOR listeners read cancelled state via a ThreadLocal set during dispatch.

rules.quote: all server-facing event definitions use `PrioritizedEvent<T>`
rules.rule: Use PrioritizedEvent<T> for all server-facing event definitions.

rules.quote: bridge layer never needs adapters
rules.rule: Do not add adapters in the bridge layer.

rules.quote: NO `rd-bridge-fabric` client-side stubs
rules.rule: Do not create client-side stubs for rd-bridge-fabric.

rules.quote: NO separate `rd-mod-loader-client` module
rules.rule: Do not create a separate rd-mod-loader-client module.

rules.quote: `rd-api` client interfaces (DrawContext, ClientEvents, GameOverlay, KeyBinding, etc.) shipped with a Fabric companion mod in rd-client that wires dispatch from RubyDungMixin hooks
rules.rule: Ship the rd-api client interfaces (DrawContext, ClientEvents, GameOverlay, KeyBinding, etc.) with a Fabric companion mod in rd-client that wires dispatch from RubyDungMixin hooks.

rules.quote: Client mods = Fabric mods, loaded by actual Fabric Loader (NOT RDForward's ModLoader)
rules.rule: Load client mods as Fabric mods via the actual Fabric Loader, not RDForward's ModLoader.

rules.quote: Cross-platform mods ship BOTH: rdmod.json (server) + fabric.mod.json (client) in same JAR or separate
rules.rule: For cross-platform mods, ship both rdmod.json for the server and fabric.mod.json for the client, either in the same JAR or separately.

rules.quote: `rd-bridge-fabric` is **server-only**
rules.rule: Keep rd-bridge-fabric server-only.

rules.quote: Hot-reload on client = Fabric's responsibility, not ours
rules.rule: Do not implement client hot-reload; leave it as Fabric's responsibility.

rules.quote: any task touching "client mod loader" or "client-side bridge" — skip.
rules.rule: Skip any task that touches a client mod loader or a client-side bridge.

rules.quote: Client mods go through real Fabric.
rules.rule: Implement client mods through real Fabric.

rules.quote: Existing static singletons removed wholesale: `CommandRegistry` (rd-server/api), `Scheduler`, `ModConfig`, `PermissionManager`, `ServerEvents.clearAll()` pattern
rules.rule: Remove the existing static singletons wholesale: CommandRegistry (rd-server/api), Scheduler, ModConfig, PermissionManager, and the ServerEvents.clearAll() pattern.

rules.quote: Replaced by rd-api interfaces + single implementation injected where needed
rules.rule: Replace those static singletons with rd-api interfaces plus a single implementation injected where needed.

rules.quote: All existing callers in `RDServer.java` (8 ServerEvents call sites, CommandRegistry.register, Scheduler.runLater, etc.) rewritten to new API in the same commits that remove the old
rules.rule: Rewrite all existing callers in RDServer.java to the new API in the same commits that remove the old API.

rules.quote: Built-in server commands (help, list, stop, tp, kick, ban, etc.) registered with `__server__` owner through new CommandRegistry interface
rules.rule: Register built-in server commands (help, list, stop, tp, kick, ban, etc.) with the __server__ owner through the new CommandRegistry interface.

rules.quote: `Scheduler.init()/reset()` lifecycle dies — scheduler is ModManager-owned instance, lifecycled with server
rules.rule: Remove the Scheduler.init()/reset() lifecycle and make the scheduler a ModManager-owned instance lifecycled with the server.

rules.quote: Existing feature classes (`BanManager`, `BlockOwnerRegistry`, `GriefProtection`, `WhitelistManager`, `TeamManager`, `ServerProperties`) stay put — they're features not API infrastructure
rules.rule: Leave existing feature classes (BanManager, BlockOwnerRegistry, GriefProtection, WhitelistManager, TeamManager, ServerProperties) in place because they are features, not API infrastructure.

rules.quote: when rewriting any of the five API utilities above, delete the old static class entirely
rules.rule: When rewriting any of the five API utilities (CommandRegistry, Scheduler, ModConfig, PermissionManager, ServerEvents), delete the old static class entirely.

rules.quote: migrate all callers in the same PR.
rules.rule: Migrate all callers in the same PR when rewriting any of those five API utilities.

rules.quote: Do NOT leave static facade shims.
rules.rule: Do not leave static facade shims when rewriting the API utilities.

rules.quote: registry class with static factory (not enum — enums can't extend)
rules.rule: Implement VersionCapability as a registry class with a static factory, not an enum, because enums cannot extend.

rules.quote: add `onPressed()` callback method
rules.rule: Add an onPressed() callback method to the KeyBinding interface.

rules.quote: add `unregister(T)` method for per-mod listener cleanup
rules.rule: Add an unregister(T) method to Event<T> for per-mod listener cleanup.

rules.quote: lives in `rd-mod-loader`, NOT rd-api
rules.rule: Place ModDescriptorParser in rd-mod-loader, not rd-api.

rules.quote: build dir has stale classes under wrong package `com.github.martinambrus.rdapi.*` (Timer, Game, ModLoader stubs) — clean before starting
rules.rule: Before starting, clean the rd-api build dir of stale classes under the wrong package com.github.martinambrus.rdapi.* (Timer, Game, ModLoader stubs).

rules.quote: Thread cleanup: interrupt + 5s join + log warning on timeout.
rules.rule: On thread cleanup, interrupt the thread, join with a 5s timeout, and log a warning on timeout.

rules.quote: NO `Thread.stop()` (removed in Java 21)
rules.rule: Do not use Thread.stop(), which was removed in Java 21.

rules.quote: old `Event`/`EventResult` classes extend new rd-api types for internal protocol callers, but rd-api is authoritative
rules.rule: Keep the old Event/EventResult classes in rd-protocol extending the new rd-api types for internal protocol callers, with rd-api as the authoritative API.

rules.quote: Core ModLoader scans `rdmod.{json,yml,toml}` only; `plugin.yml` and `fabric.mod.json` handled by their respective bridges
rules.rule: Make the Core ModLoader scan only rdmod.{json,yml,toml}; leave plugin.yml and fabric.mod.json to their respective bridges.

rules.quote: Tab completion on Alpha/Beta/pre-1.13 clients: server-side pseudo-only (no protocol support for Brigadier-style completion)
rules.rule: Implement tab completion on Alpha/Beta/pre-1.13 clients as server-side pseudo-only because there is no protocol support for Brigadier-style completion.
